source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 7.10 with Examples 7.8 and 7.9 (PDF 161-163).

blocks.text: Intensity (shiddat) us energy ki amount (miqdar) hai jo progressive (aage chalti) wave ki direction (simt) mein har second, har unit area (raqbe) se guzarti hai. Yeh wave ki power ka measure (paimana) hai aur ise aam taur par "I" se likhte hain. Is ka unit watts per square metre (W m⁻²) hai.

Progressive ya travelling (chalti hui) wave woh hai jo medium mein ek hi direction mein aage barhti hai aur energy ek jagah se doosri jagah le jati hai. Yeh stationary (standing) wave ke ulat aage chalti hai. Misalein: pani ki waves, sound waves, light waves waghaira.
Definition (tareef) ke mutabiq wave ki intensity yeh hai:

Mechanical waves (jaise sound waves, pani ki waves ya vibrate karti string ki waves) mein energy medium ke particles ki kinetic aur potential energy ki shakal mein jama hoti hai. Kitni energy jama hai, yeh particles ke mean position se displacement (amplitude) par depend karta hai. Is liye waves ki intensity I amplitude A ke square ke proportional hai:
Yahan k proportionality ka constant hai, jo wave aur medium ki physical properties (khasusiyat) par depend karta hai.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Matlab: amplitude double karein to intensity 2² = 4 guna; amplitude teen guna karein to intensity 9 guna ho jati hai.

blocks.title: Example 7.8
blocks.problem: (a) Source se 3.0 m door ek wave ki intensity 0.5 W m⁻² hai. Wave ki power kya hai? (b) Do progressive waves ki intensities 0.5 W m⁻² aur 0.25 W m⁻² hain. Dono ki total (kul) intensity nikalein.
steps: (a) Diya gaya: I = 0.5 W m⁻², r = 3.0 m; P = ?
Source har taraf barabar phailata hai, is liye area sphere ka area 4πr² hai: I = P/A = P/(4πr²).
(b) I₁ = 0.5 W m⁻², I₂ = 0.25 W m⁻²; total intensity I = I₁ + I₂ = 0.5 + 0.25.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein line “P = 0.51 × 13.04” chhapi hai. Sahi line P = 0.5 × 113.04 hai, kyunke 4 × 3.14 × (3.0)² = 113.04. Jawab 56.52 W hai, jo kitab ne bhi sahi diya hai.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Chalti hui wave ki frequency aur amplitude ek doosre se independent (azaad) hain. Isi liye aap gaane ka volume barha sakte hain (amplitude barha kar) aur us ki pitch nahi badalti, kyunke pitch frequency par depend karti hai.

blocks.prompt: Brain Teaser: kya aap us travelling wave ka decibel level nikal sakte hain jis ki intensity 10 W m⁻² hai?
blocks.explanation: Sound level (decibel) ka formula: β = 10 log₁₀(I/I₀) dB, jahan I₀ = 10⁻¹² W m⁻² sab se dheemi sunai dene wali sound (awaz) ki intensity hai. β = 10 log₁₀(10/10⁻¹²) = 10 log₁₀(10¹³) = 10 × 13 = 130 dB. Yeh dard paida karne wali bohat oonchi sound hai.

blocks.title: Example 7.9
blocks.problem: Ek speaker 50 watts power ki sound waves nikal raha hai. Agar sound waves har taraf barabar phailti hain aur speaker se 5 m door intensity naapi jaye, to intensity kya hogi agar us faasle par sphere ka (surface) area taqreeban 314 m² ho?
steps: Diya gaya: power P = 50 W, area A = 314 m² (4πr² = 4 × 3.14 × 5² = 314 m²).
Intensity = power/area: I = P/A = 50 W/314 m².

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Sound vacuum (khala) mein nahi chal sakti, kyunke wahan sound wave ko aage pohanchane wale particles hi nahi hote.

blocks.prompt: Agar wave ka amplitude teen guna ho jaye to us ki energy kitni barhti hai (MCQ 7.8)? Agar A = 2 m par I = 16 W m⁻² ho to k nikalein; agar I = 25 W m⁻² aur k = 5 W m⁻⁴ ho to A nikalein. 500 W radio antenna se 10 km door intensity kya hai (numericals 7.6, 7.8)?
blocks.explanation: I ∝ A² hai, is liye amplitude 3 guna karne se energy (intensity) 3² = 9 guna ho jati hai. k = I/A² = 16/2² = 4 W m⁻⁴. A = √(I/k) = √(25/5) = √5 ≈ 2.24 m. Antenna ke liye I = P/(4πr²) = 500/(4 × 3.14 × (10⁴)²) = 500/(1.26 × 10⁹) ≈ 4 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻².

items: Intensity: progressive wave ki direction mein per unit area, per unit time energy; I = E/(A × t) = P/A, unit W m⁻².
I = kA² (7.13): intensity amplitude ke square ke saath barhti hai; amplitude (volume) aur frequency (pitch) independent hain.
Examples: P = 56.52 W, I = 0.75 W m⁻², I ≈ 0.159 W m⁻².
